page.title: Work
page.intro: Two products I own end to end, plus supporting projects. Each case study covers the problem, the product decisions, the system behind it, the tradeoffs, and how I validated it.
caseStudy.col.question: Question
bookshelfai.tagline: Photograph a shelf; get a library.
bookshelfai.summary: A multimodal AI app that identifies every book in a photo, enriches it with structured book data, and follows it from wishlist to finished. I own it end to end — the thesis, UX, architecture, security, testing and release — building with AI development agents while making every product and technical call myself.
bookshelfai.role: Sole product owner, designer and builder
bookshelfai.problem.heading: Readers don’t want to type in their books.
bookshelfai.problem.intro: Most cataloguing apps assume one book at a time and a barcode. The real jobs were messier, and they set the product thesis.
bookshelfai.problem.item_1.title: Catalogue what I already own
bookshelfai.problem.item_1.body: Hundreds of books, no appetite for data entry.
bookshelfai.problem.item_2.title: Capture books while browsing
bookshelfai.problem.item_2.body: In a shop or a friend’s house — fast, one-handed, sometimes offline.
bookshelfai.problem.item_3.title: Scan a whole shelf at once
bookshelfai.problem.item_3.body: Spines, not barcodes. Many books per photo, reviewed in bulk.
bookshelfai.decisions.heading: Scan → identify → confirm → lifecycle.
bookshelfai.decisions.item_1.title: One scan flow, not modes
bookshelfai.decisions.item_1.body: No “cover mode” versus “shelf mode.” The model infers how many books are in frame, and a single-book photo stays the simplest case.
bookshelfai.decisions.item_2.title: Confirm before commit
bookshelfai.decisions.item_2.body: Bulk review with work-level de-duplication and partial-failure handling, so one unreadable spine never sinks a whole shelf.
bookshelfai.decisions.item_3.title: Wishlist to reading, in one place
bookshelfai.decisions.item_3.body: A book found while browsing becomes a wishlist item, then a book on the shelf, then a book read — one lifecycle instead of three apps.
bookshelfai.system.heading: Clients never talk to the model.
bookshelfai.system.intro: Server-side orchestration protects credentials, caps unauthorised model use, and keeps token cost a product decision rather than a client-side accident.
bookshelfai.system.node_1.title: Clients
bookshelfai.system.node_2.title: Edge
bookshelfai.system.node_3.title: API service
bookshelfai.system.node_4.title: Services
bookshelfai.system.node_4.detail: Vision model to identify · book-data APIs to enrich · PostgreSQL
bookshelfai.system.bullet_1: Google sign-in with RS256 access and refresh tokens, rotation and server-side revocation
bookshelfai.system.bullet_2: Rate limiting, input validation, security headers and automated security tests
bookshelfai.system.bullet_3: Bounded offline capture — scans queue safely without connectivity
bookshelfai.system.bullet_4: Separate development and production sign-in, databases and release-tagged error monitoring
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.heading: Cost, accuracy and fairness to the customer.
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.row_1.question: Which model per scan?
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.row_1.decision: A lower-cost default, with a stronger-model retry on request
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.row_1.why: Most scans don’t need the expensive model; hard ones still get it.
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.row_2.question: When does a retry cost credit?
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.row_2.decision: Only when the retry actually identifies a book
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.row_2.why: Customers shouldn’t pay for the model’s misses.
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.row_3.question: Trust the model’s titles?
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.row_3.decision: Validate against external book data and de-duplicate at the work level
bookshelfai.tradeoffs.row_3.why: Structured sources beat a plausible hallucination.
bookshelfai.validation.heading: API success isn’t experience success.
bookshelfai.validation.para_1: In testing, people missed that a scan had succeeded — the request returned fine, but the moment didn’t register. I traced the full interaction, separated functional success from UX success, and redesigned the feedback instead of calling it done.
bookshelfai.validation.para_2: When a production health check kept failing in CI, I traced it to the edge network rather than the app, separated application availability from infrastructure filtering, and questioned whether that check belonged in pull-request CI at all — instead of just silencing it.
bookshelfai.built.heading: All of it — with AI agents as the multiplier, not the decision-maker.
bc-arcade.summary: A cross-platform arcade of original games — puzzles, cards and action — built from the ground up. I own the strategy, UX, architecture, implementation, testing, release and production quality, using AI coding agents while reviewing every behaviour, test and change myself.
bc-arcade.role: Sole product owner, designer and builder
bc-arcade.problem.heading: Most casual games are designed to extract, not delight.
bc-arcade.problem.intro: The thesis: quick, genuinely fun, accessible games — without the mechanics that make the category feel predatory.
bc-arcade.problem.item_1.title: No freemium pressure
bc-arcade.problem.item_1.body: No energy meters, timers or paywalls in the middle of play. Premium is a clear purchase, not a nag.
bc-arcade.problem.item_2.title: No wagering
bc-arcade.problem.item_2.body: Stakes come from scores and objectives, never real money.
bc-arcade.problem.item_3.title: No artificial walls
bc-arcade.problem.item_3.body: No ads in the initial model; anything added later has to avoid dark patterns and disruptive placement.
bc-arcade.decisions.heading: Decisions grounded in playtests and market data.
bc-arcade.decisions.item_1.title: Rebuilt Blackjack around objectives
bc-arcade.decisions.item_1.body: Playtests showed endless-chip play had no consequence without real money, so it became a score-based arcade game with real stakes and no monetization pressure.
bc-arcade.decisions.item_2.title: Let market research shape the lineup
bc-arcade.decisions.item_2.body: Portfolio and market research surfaced gaps in the lineup — a quick sorting puzzle and a daily word game — so Sort Puzzle and Daily Word were added. Both feed the Daily Challenge: a fresh set of goals across several games every day, with streaks, that gives players a reason to come back.
bc-arcade.decisions.item_3.title: Accessibility over conformity
bc-arcade.decisions.item_3.body: When a prescribed technical pattern made screen-reader behaviour worse, I revised the shared gameplay standard instead of forcing every game to follow it.
bc-arcade.decisions.item_4.title: Tune systems, not vibes
bc-arcade.decisions.item_4.body: Hazards, enemies, difficulty and randomness are tuned against challenge, fairness, player control and replay value, with bounded, seeded randomness and explicit specs.
bc-arcade.system.heading: Quality is enforced by the pipeline, not hoped for.
bc-arcade.system.intro: About 44 CI checks, unit and Playwright end-to-end tests, and production-quality gates stand between a change and a release. Failing gates get fixed, not bypassed.
bc-arcade.system.bullet_1: An AI dependency-triage agent that merges only low-risk updates — a deterministic guard layer re-verifies authorship, file paths, CI status, branch protection and the exact commit before any merge
bc-arcade.system.bullet_2: Server-authoritative premium entitlements with signed tokens, offline grace, replay protection, restore and revocation
bc-arcade.system.bullet_3: Seeded simulations, oracle comparisons and regret metrics to evaluate non-deterministic gameplay
bc-arcade.system.bullet_4: Frame-time and render measurement, Sentry breadcrumbs and in-app feedback to separate tuning from defects
bc-arcade.tradeoffs.heading: Every automation decision has a failure mode.
bc-arcade.tradeoffs.row_1.question: How much should the AI agent merge?
bc-arcade.tradeoffs.row_1.decision: Only low-risk updates; uncertainty escalates to the higher-risk tier
bc-arcade.tradeoffs.row_1.why: Safety beats maximum automation. The AI classifies; deterministic checks decide.
bc-arcade.tradeoffs.row_2.question: How to make the app faster?
bc-arcade.tradeoffs.row_2.decision: Measure real release artifacts before removing anything
bc-arcade.tradeoffs.row_2.why: Baselines first; rejected approaches are documented when the gain isn’t worth the loss.
bc-arcade.tradeoffs.row_3.question: Where do premium features live?
bc-arcade.tradeoffs.row_3.decision: Keep hidden premium functionality from inflating store builds
bc-arcade.tradeoffs.row_3.why: Every player shouldn’t pay a download cost for features they don’t own.
bc-arcade.validation.heading: Release readiness is a product decision.
bc-arcade.validation.para_1: Randomness makes “does it work?” a statistical question. Repeatable seeded simulations, reference comparisons, blunder metrics and persona-level analysis across large samples show whether a game behaves as designed.
bc-arcade.validation.para_2: Release criteria are documented and backed by deterministic tests where they fit, security checks and performance instrumentation — and historical measurements are kept separate from current behaviour so the record stays true.
bc-arcade.built.heading: Designed and built from the ground up.
bc-arcade.built.item_5: CI quality gates and E2E testing
